claim: Coefficient route: R_inf(lambda)=sum a_n lambda^n is entire of order rho=1/(2d). Exact a_n (positive recurrence, no cancellation) Richardson-extrapolated in h=1/M^(2d-1); primary estimator is the direct 4-parameter least-squares L_n=c2*ln(n!)+c1*n+c0*ln n+c with c2->2d. Result 2d=4.0029 -> rho=0.2498 for (1,0,1); law confirmed across d=1 (2d=2.0075), d=2 (4.003), d=3 (6.00).

Eigenvalue (convergence-exponent) cross-check: R_inf(lambda)^2=prod_k(1+lambda s_k^2), order = inf{t: sum s_k^(2t)<inf}=1/p where s_k^2~k^(-p). Curvature-corrected log-log fit gives d_corr=1.9997 -> p_corr=3.9993 -> rho_prod=0.2500 for (1,0,1); agrees with the coefficient route (0.2498) and across d=1 (rho 0.500), d=2 (0.250), d=3 (0.1667). The two independent routes agree.

Genus p*=0. Zeros lambda_k=-1/s_k^2; sum |1/lambda_k|=sum s_k^2=Tr T^2 = S < inf (trace-class), so the smallest integer with sum s_k^(2(p+1))<inf is p*=0 and the Hadamard product R_inf^2=prod_k(1+lambda s_k^2) carries NO exponential factor. Numerically sum s_k^2 (spectral) = 0.13066962 = S (direct) to 8 digits for (1,0,1). Rests only on sum u_n<inf.

Rigorous by-hand order bracket rho=1/(2d): (i) entire order<=1 from a_n<=S^n/n! (non-sparse overcount, dominated by exp(S|lambda|)); (ii) lower rho>=1/(2d) from the single dominant sparse term a_n>=prod_{k<=n}u_{2k} with u_{2k}~(2k)^(-2d) giving log(1/a_n)~2d n log n; (iii) upper rho<=1/(2d) from a_n<=e_n (coeffs of canonical product prod_{i>=2}(1+lambda u_i)) whose order = convergence exponent inf{t:sum u_i^t<inf}=1/(2d). (i),(ii) elementary; (iii) cites the standard canonical-product theorem.

Theorem-4 soft spot. Telescoping bound S=sum_{n>=2}u_n <= 1/((3A+B)(A+B+C)) (since u_k=1/(b(k)-b(k-1))*(1/b(k-1)-1/b(k)), b(k)-b(k-1)=A(2k-1)+B>=3A+B). On the INTEGER family A,C>=1,B>=0 the denominator is >=6, so S<=1/6<1 UNCONDITIONALLY (grid A,C in 1..5,B in 0..4: all 125 triples S<=1/6, max S=0.1306696 at the running family (1,0,1), the extremal lattice point).
